_comment: Agent registry — the Agency-native replacement for clawndom's AGENTS_CONFIG. Maps a dispatching agentName to the repo Builder may modify, the path within it that scopes Builder's edits, the base ref, branch convention, the reviewer named for review-required PRs, and the verification command run before a PR is marked ready.
_codeOwners_comment: Code owners for THIS deployed Agency instance — the GitHub handles Builder requests as reviewers on every review-required PR (forged tools + structural workspace changes). The single source of truth for who reviews lives here, in the instance config — not in per-repo CODEOWNERS files that drift.

_toolRepo._comment: The shared tool library Builder forges new tools into (see prompt 'What goes where'). Not a dispatching agent — the target repo + verify command for a tool PR. Tool PRs are always review-required (a tool is added files + a tool.yaml, which the auto-merge gate holds for human review).

_runtimeRepo._comment: The Agency runtime itself — the Rust daemon every agent runs on. Not a dispatching agent. Builder PRs here when a bug's root cause (or a requested change) is in the platform, not an agent's workspace or a tool: transport (Slack/webhook intake), routing engine, queue/worker, inbound de-duplication, secrets resolution. Highest blast radius (every agent runs this code), so runtime PRs are ALWAYS review-required and must pass the full make-check gate (clippy + tests + 90% coverage + security + naming) locally before being marked testable.

_builderRepo._comment: Builder's OWN workspace — its prompt, templates, agency.yaml, and this registry. Not a dispatching agent. Builder PRs here when a bug's root cause is in its own behavior/config (e.g. it didn't acknowledge reviewer feedback before reworking, or it cloned outside its ephemeral cwd). Lives in the engineering-agents monorepo alongside Patch/Scarlett. ALWAYS review-required; never self-edit on the box. Resolving this entry is what lets Builder improve itself through the same reviewed-PR path as everything else.
